description: We are Merge Masters, building a robust, offline-first health monitoring software system to track astronaut vitals and automate deep-space medical triage. Looking for developers and UI/UX designers passionate about clean dashboards, data visualization, and space exploration.
summary:
ASTRAHEALTH is a health monitoring and decision support tool for astronauts on long duration missions. Due to the hazardous nature of deep space exploration astronauts are exposed to high health risks due to radiation, micro gravity and isolation. On Earth astronauts do not have real-time medical support.

ASTRAHEALTH provides real-time, non-contact health monitoring using computer vision and local personalised health data. ASTRA VISION can be applied to cameras on board the spacecraft or cabin. ASTRA VISION uses rPPG and facial and body landmarks to provide real-time non-invasive estimation of heart rate, respiratory rate, eye blinks to indicate fatigue and physical activity. ASTRAHEALTH compares real-time health data from the camera, wearables or wellness application to the personalised baselines. It has been designed with an Earth Communication Delay Mode so that all health data is processed locally to protect astronauts’ health data. Health data will be stored and reports will be made on priority for flight surgeons once communication is regained. This enables autonomous proactive health care for astronauts on future Lunar and Mars missions.
details:
ASTRAHEALTH is an intelligent, mobile-first health monitoring platform designed to help astronauts monitor their physical and mental health during long-duration space missions. Space environments expose astronauts to several health risks, including radiation, microgravity, isolation, sleep disturbances and cardiovascular changes. Since immediate medical assistance from Earth may not always be available, our aim is to make health monitoring easier, more accessible and proactive.

The platform allows astronauts to register their health information, record vital measurements, monitor sleep and wellness, and compare their current health indicators with their personal pre-mission baseline. It helps identify unusual changes over time and provides understandable health insights and recommendations so astronauts can take appropriate preventive action.

One of our main innovations is ASTRA VISION, a camera-based contactless health monitoring feature. Instead of depending entirely on manual measurements, it explores how cameras inside spacecraft, or dedicated cameras installed in crew areas, could support health monitoring through computer vision. By analyzing facial landmarks and specific regions such as the forehead, cheeks and eyes, the system explores experimental heart-rate estimation using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG), along with fatigue-related indicators. It also includes visual tracking of chest and shoulder movements for experimental breathing-rate estimation and posture analysis. This could make routine health observations less dependent on manual input. Our current prototype demonstrates camera access, facial landmark detection, tracking regions and camera quality assessment, while integration with actual spacecraft camera infrastructure is a future deployment possibility.

ASTRAHEALTH also considers the challenges of communication delays during deep-space missions. Its offline-first approach is designed to preserve health records when connectivity is unavailable and prepare medical summaries that can be shared with medical teams when communication becomes possible. Other features include space hazard monitoring, mental wellness assessments, health trend visualization, preventive health recommendations and medical report generation.

We developed the application using modern web technologies, including Next.js, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS and browser-based computer vision technologies. We also use Firebase for authentication and are developing persistent health data management and offline capabilities using appropriate backend and browser storage technologies.

What makes ASTRAHEALTH creative is that it brings personal health monitoring, camera-assisted observations, baseline intelligence and space mission awareness together in one platform. Rather than simply displaying health numbers, our goal is to help astronauts understand changes in their health and know when further attention may be needed.

While developing the project, we considered the unique conditions of space missions, including microgravity, limited medical resources, communication delays, data privacy, ease of use and the reliability of measurements. We also recognize that camera-based estimates are experimental and cannot replace dedicated medical instruments or professional medical assessment.

Our ultimate goal is to support safer and healthier human exploration beyond Earth, especially during future long-duration lunar and Mars missions.
